t:
How many of the following can be identified using ‘Layer Test’.
(A) F⁻
(B) Cl⁻
(C) Br⁻
(D) I⁻
s:
Layer test is for bromide and iodide only, where, to the solution chlorine water is added; if solution has bromide, it is oxidized to free bromine and if the solution has iodide, it is oxidized to free iodine. If to test solution some CCl₄ is added, that remains as a separate layer and into this liberated bromine /iodine is dissolved and gives the organic layer red orange colour and violet colour respectively. Cl₂(aq)+2Br⁻(aq)→2Cl⁻(aq)+
Br₂ (red- orange colour) Cl₂(aq)+2I⁻(aq)→2Cl⁻(aq)+
I₂ (violet)

s: Na₂HPO₄ precipitates Mg²⁺ (group VI) (A–q); H₂S in NH₄OH is group IV reagent (Ni²⁺) (B–p); NH₄OH/NH₄Cl is group III reagent (Al³⁺) (C–s); H₂S in dil. HCl is group II reagent (Pb²⁺) (D–r).

t: A solution containing As³⁺,Cd²⁺,Ni²⁺ and Zn²⁺ is made alkaline with dilute NH₄OH and treated with H₂S. The precipitate obtained will consist of
s:
As³⁺ and Cd²⁺ are the radicals of group II, whereas Ni²⁺&Zn²⁺ are the radicals of group IV. The solubility product of group IV radicals is higher as compared to group II. NH₄OH increases the ionisation of H₂S
by removing H⁺of H₂S as unionisable water. H₂S⇌2H⁺+S²⁻;H⁺+OH⁻→H₂O
Thus excess of sulphide ions are present which leads to the precipitation of all the four ions. Note : HCl decreases ionisation of H₂S
whereas NH₄OH increases the ionisation of H₂S.
